title: Two-tier parameter staging and eviction playbook
content:
Purpose:
This playbook describes a two-tier parameter residency strategy for large model serving that balances latency SLOs and constrained device memory. It outlines a staged file mapping and NVMe-backed spill lane, small on-device microcache (hotset slab) for kernel-affine weights, an eviction/prefetch policy tuned for multi-tenant batches, CRC-verified atomic staging and rollback semantics, and telemetry/QA to validate correctness and economics.

Goals (non-exhaustive):
- Keep tail latency under per-request SLO during typical interactive traffic while maximizing effective memory utilization.
- Allow progressive, per-layer parameter fetch so early tokens can be produced while later layers stream in.
- Provide safe atomic replacement and fast rollback for model swaps and in-flight hotpatch updates.
- Expose observable knobs for optimizer and operators (prefetch budget, hotset size, spill threshold, async priority).

High-level design summary:
1) Residency lanes:
   - Resident slab (RAM/GPU): small, kernel-friendly on-device memory for most frequently accessed tensors (hotset). Kernel scheduler pins these when executing hot paths.
   - Staging lane (memory-mapped views + transient buffers): memory-mapped files backed by a managed file cache; supports partial mapping at a page granularity with optional compressed blobs on disk.
   - Spill lane (NVMe): persistent local SSD store for cold parameters and larger uncompressed shards; supports sequential prefetch into staging lane.

2) Progressive fetch and execution flow:
   - On request arrival, allocator asks residency controller for model version and access plan.
   - Controller returns a prioritized list of parameter fragments (coarse-grained layers -> fine-grained tiles) and a schedule for fetching.
   - Runtime executes earliest-ready layers using parameters already resident; later layers begin execution when corresponding fragments arrive.
   - KV cache policy integrates by pinning KV-related weights during attention-heavy windows to avoid eviction churn.

3) Atomic staging and swap protocol (for model updates/hotpatch):
   - New parameters are staged into a write-once directory with content-addressed filenames and CRC32/sha256 manifests.
   - Staging completes when all required fragments are validated; an atomic symlink switch (or metadata commit) points the runtime at the new version.
   - If validation fails or in-flight requests require fallback, rollback uses the previous symlink target; transient memory mappings are unmapped and freed in a controlled quiesce window.

4) Eviction and prefetch policy:
   - Two-level LRU with weighted recency: microcache (hot slab) uses a strict LRU with per-tensor cost accounting. Staging lane uses a segmented LRU tuned to sequential layer access patterns.
   - Affinity buckets: tensors are coalesced into affinity buckets (by layer, attention block, or kernel dependency) to evict whole buckets rather than fragmenting kernels.
   - Prefetch hints: profiler and telemetry feed a small ML model (on-controller) that predicts next-k-tensors; controller sends prefetch hints to staging and spill managers.
   - Tenancy fairness: budgets per-tenant ensure one noisy workload cannot starve others; admission control rejects prefetch requests if tenant budget exceeded.

5) Kernel-aware residency:
   - Runtime exposes APIs to kernels indicating "required in-hotset" vs "ok-in-staging" for each tensor.
   - For fused/eager kernels that access many tensors, allocator can bump priority or temporarily pin entire affinity bucket.

6) CRC and integrity checks:
   - Each fragment stores CRC32 and a sha256 in the manifest.
   - On open/mmap, file pages are validated lazily on first access via a background worker; critical pages required by the executing kernel are validated synchronously.

Operational APIs (sketch):
- residencyController.requestPlan(modelId, version, requestId, priority) -> {fragments: [{id, offset, size, affinity_bucket}], prefetchBudget}  // synchronous
- stagingManager.prefetch(fragmentId, priority, targetLane) -> future
- spillManager.fetchToStaging(shardId, byteRange) -> future
- residencyController.commitSwap(versionId) -> {success|failed, rollbackToken}
- residencyController.pinAffinity(bucketId, ttlMs)
- telemetry.emit("residency.fragment.latency", {fragment, durationMs})

Failure modes and mitigations:
- Partial fragment corruption: detected via CRC on access -> mark fragment suspicious, try redundant fetch from remote cache, if unavailable, fall back to CPU-emulation path or degrade to a smaller compatible model variant. Emit alert with requestId and fragment id.
- Staging race during swap: if execution holds a mmap view while commit occurs, commit must record reference counts and defer unmap until quiesce bound or force-unmap after timeout with emergency rollback that restarts affected requests.
- NVMe device outage: fallback to remote pull (S3) with admission control; degrade concurrency to protect cores and network egress.

Telemetry & SLOs to collect (examples):
- per-fragment fetch latency (p50/p95/p99)
- hotset hit ratio and hotset eviction rate
- per-request early-continue fraction (percentage of requests that returned first token before all fragments arrived)
- number of rollback events per hour and average rollback duration
- NVMe read throughput and stall count
- kernel stalls due to missing parameters (counts)

Testing checklist (QA and stage):
- Unit: fragment manifest validation, CRC mismatch handling, walleted staging commit/rollback sequence emulation.
- Integration: synthetic traffic with layered access patterns (attention-heavy vs ff-heavy) and quantize effect on hotset size.
- Fault injection: drop NVMe, corrupt one fragment file, slow disks, preemption during commit, simultaneous multi-tenant spike.
- Perf: measure p99 latency under backpressure with and without prefetch ML model enabled; validate tail improvement vs cost.

Implementation notes and heuristics (practical knobs):
- Default hotset budget: 4–12% of model parameters (configurable per-deployment). Start small and let telemetry increase gradually.
- Fragment granularity: 256KB–2MB fragments; bias smaller for attention heads, larger for dense FFN weights.
- Prefetch concurrency: limit to ~8x device cores to avoid IO saturation on typical instances.
- Admission thresholds: when staging queue > 75% capacity, drop low-priority prefetches and prioritize kernel-essential fragments.

Open questions and follow-ups:
- Should we integrate block-level deduplication across model versions to reduce NVMe footprint? (tradeoff: CPU/metadata overhead)
- What is the optimal feature set for the prefetch predictor given telemetry bandwidth constraints?
- How to expose graceful degradation primitives to application teams (e.g., soft-fail to fallback model variant vs raise 5xx)?

Appendix: quick scenario walkthrough
- Cold start, model vA: controller identifies largest FFN shards as cold; runtime requests earliest attention-layer fragments first, loads into staging, validates, pins top-k attention heads into hotset; request 1 can produce token 0 after attention head params arrive; background pulls rest of layers.
- Hotpatch to vB during traffic: new fragments are staged to write-once path; once validated, commitSwap updates model pointer; in-flight requests continue to use previous mapping until their refcounts drop; new requests use vB. If a critical integrity error is detected during staging, rollbackToken triggers a safe revert and evacuation of new mappings.

Appendix B: short glossary
- fragment: contiguous slice of checkpoint used as atomic fetch unit
- hotset: on-device, kernel-pinned residency slab for latency-sensitive tensors
- staging: transient mmap/heap views backed by local file cache
- spill: NVMe-resident cold-store for large shards

Notes to reviewers:
- This playbook focuses on practical engineering tradeoffs rather than exploring fully-distributed parameter shards. It assumes a single-box per-inference-worker model.
- I'm iterating on eviction heuristics; please call out any real-world request patterns (from profiler) that break the affinity-bucket assumption.

Action items:
- (Asha) Prototype manifest + atomic-commit path, add CRC validation hooks to stagingManager (2w)
- (Noah) Implement telemetry counters and minimal prefetch predictor baseline (3w)
- (María) Write integration tests for hotpatch commit/rollback (2w)
- (Eliot) Run perf sweep on c6i-equivalent NVMe-backed instances and report p99 changes (1w)

References and inspiration:
- internal: CONFLUENCE:serving-runtime/param-staging-v1
- external: streaming-weight-papers, mmap best-practices, kernel-affinity scheduling notes

End of playbook.
